The slope fitter (tools/scaling.py) is a gate: 10 deliberate mutations, all detected - seven for its scope refusals and interval labelling, and three added 2026-09-02 when it took over the cluster bootstrap that 0011's slope clause gates on: clustered evaluation rows must widen the interval and be labelled 'cluster', a groups array that does not match the evaluation set is refused, and fewer than four rungs is refused.

The byte-identity collision ceiling barely moves with carve size: 20.9125 distinct streams of 26 at a 4096-byte window against 20.79 at 512, over 400 source chunks whose seeds are disjoint from every training corpus. Whatever fails at a shorter carve is therefore a modelling limit, not an information limit.

claims.claim: The 1024-byte failure is not localised to any feature family: at a matched 100000 rung every one of six feature subsets degrades from 4096 to 1024 by a ratio between 0.5895 and 0.6275, a spread of 0.038. Law L4: a representation made of summary statistics over a fragment binds the result to the fragment length. The 1024/4096 degradation ratio has a spread of 0.038 across six feature subsets - uniform, with no family surviving and none dying.

Conjecture C1: withholding the transform's input is what creates the white space for a transform label factory, and is the same property that makes its market a forensics market and therefore small. Explicitly a conjecture, not a measured law.
claims.why_not_verifiable: It is an argued reading of this repository's own search record - our search, our framing, our blind spots - and not a measurement. No artifact can establish it and none is claimed to. It is filed in the weakest class and labelled C1 rather than L5 so it can never be quoted alongside the four measured laws. The document states what would falsify it: a transform label factory whose input is withheld by privacy, regulation, physics or commercial boundary rather than by after-the-fact loss.

claims.claim: The C1 falsifier-search gate of preregistration 0008 is shown capable of failing by 14 deliberate mutations, all detected - including one asserting that a search too narrow to conclude anything VOIDS rather than returning a comforting negative, and one asserting that finding no falsifier does not promote the conjecture.
Preregistration 0008 hunted C1's own stated falsifier across 14 candidates spanning all four non-loss withholding modes, default posture REJECT, and returned NO_FALSIFIER_FOUND. 0 candidates cleared.

Refinement of C1: deliberate withholding is documented withholding. Where an institution withholds a transform's input on purpose, disclosure norms make it publish what it did - the placeholder format, the created_by string, the epsilon, the FITS header - so the label ships with the artifact. The label is hidden only where the withholding was accidental, and accidental withholding is loss, which is the forensics case C1 describes.
claims.why_not_verifiable: An argued reading of 14 screened candidates, not a measurement. Filed with C1 in the weakest class. Its falsifier: an institution that deliberately withholds an input while publishing the artifact and NOT documenting the transform.

claims.claim: Conjecture C2: G2 and G5 pull against each other. A free label manufacturer requires POSSESSING the transform; possessing it means it is open or commoditised; and the provenance of a commoditised transform's output is usually worth little to know. Its falsifier exists - TLS stack identification - and is solved by JA3/JA4, a hash rather than a learned model, which is law L3(i) arriving from the other direction.
claims.why_not_verifiable: Argument, not measurement. Filed in the weakest class with C1 and its refinement. VERDICT.md caps this deliberately: the next round that matters is a MEASUREMENT breaking one of the three tensions, not a fourth conjecture explaining why they hold.

claims.claim: The byte-representation gate of preregistration 0009 is shown capable of failing by 10 deliberate mutations, all detected - including one asserting that clearing the A2 margin while LOSING to the model it replaces is rejected, and one asserting that a negative is reported as strengthening L4 rather than as inconclusive.

A byte-sequence CNN over raw 1024-byte fragments reaches 0.0849 at the matched 100000 rung - below the 0.0943 of logistic regression on a plain byte histogram, and below the 0.1165 of the hand-engineered feature model it was meant to replace. Seeing byte order did worse than counting bytes. Verdict BYTE_MODEL_FAILS.

RETRACTED READING, kept for the record: 0009 read its null control's 0.0006 loss movement as evidence the model was too small. A probe shows the cause is the global average pool, which averages away per-example identity - a flatten head at identical convolutional capacity memorises 5000 shuffled labels to 0.364 train accuracy where the pooled head reaches 0.0486. Filed in CORRECTIONS.md.

A null control the model cannot fail carries no information. With a global average pool the network reaches only 0.0486 train accuracy on 5000 shuffled labels after 30 epochs, against 0.0385 chance - so 0009's clean null control was guaranteed by architecture rather than earned. This is the mutation-testing argument, which this repository already made about gates, applied to controls.

The position-preserving-head gate of preregistration 0010 is shown capable of failing by 12 deliberate mutations, all detected - including one rejecting a null control that is clean but UNFAILABLE, and one asserting such a run is named inconclusive rather than counted as a negative.

Preregistration 0010's flatten-head model reaches 0.0385 - exactly chance - on real labels under the recipe frozen from 0009, and 0.0393 train accuracy on shuffled labels, so its null control never became failable and the frozen reader names the round inconclusive on the exact point it exists to settle.

Methodological finding from 0010: 'change only the head' was chosen for attributability, and it is what made the round inconclusive - a training recipe tuned under one architecture is not architecture-neutral, so freezing it privileges the incumbent. A fair comparison must preregister a recipe search per architecture.
claims.why_not_verifiable: An inference from one inconclusive run, not a measurement. Filed in the weakest class; its test - a preregistered per-head recipe search - is stated and was not run in this container.

principle: Three classes. The weakest is printed first and loudest, because the value of a coverage map is entirely in its worst row.
